note: The minor arpeggio found inside the minor pentatonic scale: the position with the chord's three notes ringed, then the arpeggio drawn on its own. One position is on the screen, so the title names no number; moves holds any key, so the title and text name the key as a param and the chord as a token.

exercise.title: The minor arpeggio inside {{=key}} minor pentatonic
exercise.why: The notes of the minor chord on the root are three of the five notes of the minor pentatonic scale, so the arpeggio is already inside the position: leave two notes out.

cells.text: The neck below shows the {{=key}} minor pentatonic scale in one position, and the ringed dots are the notes of {{chord:i}}: {{1}}, {{b3}} and {{5}}. Start on the lowest ringed {{1}} and play only the ringed notes up to the high e string and back down, leaving the other two notes of the scale out.

Now the same arpeggio drawn on its own, with the rest of the scale gone. Play it up and back down from the lowest {{1}}.
Practice until you can start on any ringed {{1}} and go up or down.
{{?key}}In another key the arpeggio sits on other frets, and it is still the three ringed notes inside the same position.
